$comment: The Radix surface this kit intends to match, one entry per behaviour.
A behaviour counts as MATCHED only when a spec exercises it and every
observation in that spec agrees with Radix. Behaviours with no spec are
reported as UNCOVERED — the catalogue is the denominator, so adding a
component here lowers the score until the work is actually done.

behaviours.focus-on-click: clicking moves focus to the control
behaviours.disabled-blur: clicking a disabled control drops focus
behaviours.aria-pressed: pressed state is exposed as aria-pressed

behaviours.pointer-toggle: clicking the trigger opens and closes
behaviours.keyboard-toggle: Enter and Space toggle while the trigger is focused
behaviours.state-attr: root, trigger and content all carry the state
behaviours.wrapper-role: the root carries no ARIA role of its own

behaviours.indeterminate: the mixed state is exposed as aria-checked=mixed
behaviours.indeterminate-clears: activating from mixed goes to checked

behaviours.pointer-select: clicking an item selects it and deselects the rest
behaviours.roving-focus: only the selected item is in the tab order
behaviours.arrow-next: ArrowDown/ArrowRight moves selection to the next item
behaviours.arrow-prev: ArrowUp/ArrowLeft moves selection to the previous item
behaviours.arrow-wraps: arrow movement wraps at the ends
behaviours.group-role: the root exposes the radiogroup role
behaviours.disabled-skipped: a disabled item is skipped by arrow movement

arrow-selects.note: selection follows arrow focus, per the WAI-ARIA radio pattern
arrow-selects.disputed: The reference does not do this consistently. Measured on @radix-ui/react-radio-group in Chromium, settled two frames AND 500ms: the first two arrow presses after a pointer click move focus without moving selection, and every press after that moves both. Reproduced with a 2-item and a 3-item group, and with the React root on #root and on document.body. Until it is decided whether to follow the spec or the reference, this stays uncovered rather than being scored either way.

behaviours.arrow-next: ArrowRight moves to the next tab
behaviours.arrow-prev: ArrowLeft moves to the previous tab
behaviours.arrow-wraps: arrow movement wraps at the ends
behaviours.panel-swap: only the active tab's panel is reachable
behaviours.list-role: the list exposes tablist and items expose tab
behaviours.disabled-skipped: a disabled tab is skipped by arrow movement

behaviours.single-open: opening one item closes the previously open one
behaviours.pointer-toggle: clicking a header toggles its item

behaviours.switch-role: the control exposes the switch role

behaviours.keyboard-open: Enter on the trigger opens it
behaviours.focus-into: opening moves focus into the dialog
behaviours.focus-restore: closing returns focus to the trigger
behaviours.aria-expanded: the trigger says whether it is showing
behaviours.background-hidden: everything outside is out of the accessibility tree
behaviours.content-unmounted: closed content is not in the tree at all

focus-trap.note: Tab and Shift+Tab cycle inside the open dialog
focus-trap.disputed: No spec can prove this yet: the harness has no Tab step, and UiHost has no document-order focus model to answer one with. Catalogued so the gap is counted rather than assumed away — see PLAN.md.

behaviours.no-role: a label carries no ARIA role of its own
behaviours.renders-text: its text is present and visible

behaviours.decorative-drops-role: a decorative separator reports no role at all
behaviours.orientation: vertical and horizontal both lay out

behaviours.state-loading: a value below the maximum reads as loading
behaviours.state-indeterminate: no value at all reads as indeterminate
behaviours.indicator: the indicator carries the same state

behaviours.no-role: pure layout: nothing in it carries a role
behaviours.ratio-applied: the inner box takes the declared ratio

behaviours.button-role: the control around the icon is a button
behaviours.label-names-it: the hidden label is its accessible name
behaviours.glyph-hidden: the glyph is decoration and does not reach the name

behaviours.no-role: neither the root nor the fallback carries a role
behaviours.fallback-shown: with no image the fallback is what is there

behaviours.radiogroup-role: a single-select group IS a radio group
behaviours.pointer-select: clicking an item selects it and deselects the rest
behaviours.roving-focus: exactly one item is a tab stop
behaviours.arrow-next: arrows move focus to the next item
behaviours.arrow-wraps: arrow movement wraps at the ends

behaviours.toolbar-role: the root exposes the toolbar role
behaviours.roving-focus: exactly one button is a tab stop
behaviours.arrow-next: ArrowRight moves focus to the next button
behaviours.arrow-wraps: arrow movement wraps at the ends

behaviours.alertdialog-role: the content is an alertdialog, not a dialog
behaviours.focus-cancel: opening moves focus to Cancel, not to the destructive action
behaviours.focus-restore: closing returns focus to the trigger
behaviours.background-hidden: everything outside is out of the accessibility tree
behaviours.content-unmounted: closed content is not in the tree at all

behaviours.pointer-close: clicking the open trigger closes it again
behaviours.not-modal: the page behind stays in the accessibility tree
behaviours.focus-into: opening moves focus to the first focusable node inside
behaviours.focus-restore: closing returns focus to the trigger
behaviours.aria-expanded: the trigger says whether it is showing
behaviours.content-unmounted: closed content is not in the tree at all

behaviours.hover-opens: the pointer arriving on the trigger opens it
behaviours.tooltip-role: the content carries the tooltip role
behaviours.escape-closes: Escape closes it and leaves focus alone
behaviours.content-unmounted: a closed tip is not in the tree at all

behaviours.hover-opens: the pointer arriving on the trigger opens it
behaviours.link-trigger: the trigger is a link, not a button
behaviours.content-no-role: the card itself carries no role
behaviours.content-unmounted: a closed card is not in the tree at all

behaviours.menu-role: the surface is a menu and its children are menuitems
behaviours.focus-content: opening focuses the surface, not the first item
behaviours.arrow-first: ArrowDown from the surface focuses the first item
behaviours.arrow-last: ArrowUp from the surface focuses the last item
behaviours.no-wrap: arrows stop at the ends rather than wrapping
behaviours.item-closes: activating an item closes the menu
behaviours.focus-restore: closing returns focus to the trigger
behaviours.background-hidden: everything outside is out of the accessibility tree
behaviours.content-unmounted: a closed menu is not in the tree at all
behaviours.sub-haspopup: a row that opens a submenu says so with aria-haspopup
behaviours.sub-trigger-role: a sub-trigger is a menuitem, with an expanded state of its own
behaviours.sub-right-opens: ArrowRight on a sub-trigger opens its submenu
behaviours.sub-first-item: opening a submenu by name puts focus on its FIRST item, unlike opening the root menu
behaviours.sub-left-closes: ArrowLeft closes the submenu and returns focus to the sub-trigger
behaviours.sub-left-unwinds-one: ArrowLeft unwinds one level, not all of them
behaviours.sub-nested: a submenu may itself contain one
behaviours.sub-disabled: a disabled sub-trigger is skipped and opens nothing
behaviours.sub-escape-closes-all: Escape closes every level at once and returns focus to the trigger
behaviours.sub-hover-opens: resting the pointer on a sub-trigger opens it after 100ms, leaving focus on the row
behaviours.sub-hover-away-closes: moving the pointer to another row closes it at once — slow to open, instant to close
behaviours.sub-content-menu: the submenu surface is a menu whose children are menuitems
behaviours.sub-item-closes-all: choosing a leaf at any depth closes the whole menu

behaviours.secondary-open: the secondary pointer button opens it
behaviours.trigger-no-role: the trigger has no role and no name
behaviours.menu-role: the surface is a menu and its children are menuitems
behaviours.focus-content: opening focuses the surface, not the first item
behaviours.arrow-steps: arrows step between items, skipping disabled ones
behaviours.focus-lost: closing leaves focus nowhere, because the trigger cannot take it
behaviours.background-hidden: everything outside is out of the accessibility tree

behaviours.slider-role: the thumb is the slider, and the only tab stop
behaviours.value-reported: the position and the range are announced as numbers
behaviours.arrow-increment: Right and Up add a step
behaviours.arrow-decrement: Left and Down subtract a step
behaviours.home-end: Home goes to the minimum and End to the maximum
behaviours.clamped: the value never leaves the range
behaviours.disabled-inert: a disabled slider takes neither focus nor keys
behaviours.pointer-jump: pressing the track moves the value to that point
behaviours.pointer-drag: holding and moving keeps the value under the cursor
behaviours.drag-clamped: dragging past an end stops at it
behaviours.pointer-focuses-thumb: a press on the rail focuses the thumb, not the rail
behaviours.step-snapped: a dragged value lands on the step grid

behaviours.no-focus-steal: raising one does not move focus
behaviours.tab-reachable: the raised toast is a tab stop
behaviours.focus-viewport: dismissing moves focus to the viewport
behaviours.content-unmounted: an unraised toast is not in the tree at all

sortable.$comment: Not Radix — Radix has no sortable. ReUI's, and every shadcn-family one, is dnd-kit underneath, so dnd-kit is the oracle.

behaviours.sortable-roledescription: every item says it is sortable, so a reader learns the affordance
behaviours.sortable-pointer-reorder: dragging an item onto another reorders the list on release
behaviours.sortable-keyboard-pickup: Space picks the focused item up
behaviours.sortable-keyboard-move: arrows move the picked-up item between positions
behaviours.sortable-keyboard-drop: Space drops it where it now is
behaviours.sortable-escape-cancels: Escape puts it back and reorders nothing
behaviours.sortable-announces: every stage is announced into a live region

behaviours.menubar-role: the bar is a menubar and its triggers are menu items
behaviours.menubar-pointer-open: clicking a trigger opens its menu and focuses the content
behaviours.menubar-item-closes: choosing a row closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger
behaviours.menubar-arrow-between-menus: an arrow moves which menu is OPEN, not which trigger has focus
behaviours.menubar-arrow-into-items: an arrow from the content focuses the first row
behaviours.menubar-escape-closes: Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger
behaviours.menubar-roving-tabstop: the bar holds the tab stop until a menu has been opened

behaviours.select-roles: the trigger is a combobox, the list a listbox and the rows options
behaviours.select-pointer-open: clicking the trigger opens the list and focuses the CHOSEN option
behaviours.select-choose-value: choosing an option closes the list and returns focus to the trigger
behaviours.select-selected-state: exactly one option is selected, and the rest say they are not

behaviours.navmenu-roles: the triggers are buttons and the panel holds links
behaviours.navmenu-pointer-open: clicking a trigger opens its panel and leaves focus on the trigger
behaviours.navmenu-every-trigger-tabbable: every trigger is a tab stop — there is no roving focus

scrollarea.$comment: Measured: the reference exposes NO roles and no names here, and renders no scrollbar until the pointer is over it. What is observable is that the content stays reachable and visible while the box does not grow.

behaviours.scrollarea-roles: nothing is given a role the reference does not give it
behaviours.scrollarea-content-reachable: the content is in the tree and visible even though it does not fit

tree.$comment: Not Radix — Radix has no tree. ReUI's is @headless-tree/react over @headless-tree/core with syncDataLoaderFeature and hotkeysCoreFeature, so headless-tree is the oracle. It contributes the roles, the level/size/position numbers and the whole key map; the example wires NO selection feature, so every row reports aria-selected=false and stays that way. Measured in specs/tree_*.json against the library itself. DRAG AND DROP is a third mode ("dnd": true), in two halves. The KEYBOARD half walks drop targets an arrow at a time; the POINTER half computes one from where in a row the cursor sits, driven by synthetic HTML5 DragEvents because Playwright cannot drive native drag through the mouse. Neither half is observable in a DOM trace at all — the page looks identical from one arrow press to the next — so both are captured into oracle/tree-dnd.json and checked by `npm run ui:tree:dnd:check`, the way the table's state machine is. SELECTION IS A MODE: everything up to `selected-false` is measured with selectionFeature OFF, which is ReUI's configuration and must stay that way; everything from `selected-state` on is the same library with the feature ON, and is a different contract — a fixture asks for it with "selection": true.

behaviours.tree-role: the container is a tree and the root item is not a row in it
behaviours.treeitem-role: every visible row is a treeitem, folder or leaf alike
behaviours.level: each row says how deep it sits, counting the invisible root as level 0
behaviours.setsize: each row says how many siblings share its parent
behaviours.setpos: each row says which of those siblings it is
behaviours.arrow-steps: Down and Up step through the VISIBLE rows, crossing in and out of open folders
behaviours.right-expands: ArrowRight on a closed folder opens it and stays put
behaviours.right-enters: ArrowRight on an already-open folder steps to its first child
behaviours.right-leaf-steps: ArrowRight on a leaf is not a no-op — it steps DOWN, the same as an open folder
behaviours.left-collapses: ArrowLeft on an open folder closes it and stays put
behaviours.left-to-parent: ArrowLeft on a leaf or a closed folder steps to the parent
behaviours.left-top-level-noop: ArrowLeft at the top level goes nowhere, because the root is not a row
behaviours.home: Home focuses the first visible row
behaviours.end: End focuses the LAST visible row, which is the deepest open descendant and not the last top-level item
behaviours.no-wrap: arrows stop at the ends rather than wrapping
behaviours.enter-toggles: Enter opens or closes the focused folder
behaviours.space-toggles: Space does the same as Enter — with no selection feature it selects nothing
behaviours.selected-false: every row exposes aria-selected=false, including the focused one
behaviours.selected-state: a selected row says aria-selected=true and the rest say false
behaviours.select-click: a plain click makes that row the whole selection
behaviours.select-ctrl-click: Ctrl-click adds a row, and Ctrl-clicking it again takes it away
behaviours.select-shift-click: Shift-click selects the range between the anchor and this row
behaviours.select-anchor: the anchor is moved by any click that is NOT a shift-click, so two shift-clicks in a row extend from the same place
behaviours.select-modified-click-does-not-toggle: a click with Shift or Ctrl held focuses and selects but does NOT open or close a folder — otherwise shift-clicking down a list would open every folder on the way
behaviours.select-shift-arrow: Shift+Arrow selects the next row and moves focus onto it
behaviours.select-shift-shrinks: when the focused row and the next one are BOTH selected, Shift+Arrow deselects the one being left — so walking back over a range gives the range back
behaviours.select-ends: Shift+Arrow at an end changes neither selection nor focus
behaviours.select-all-is-visible-only: and everything means the VISIBLE rows — a collapsed folder's children are not selected, which shows when it is opened
behaviours.select-space-still-toggles: Space still opens and closes a folder, because it is commented out of the library's selection hotkeys
behaviours.select-enter-collapses: Enter and Space also set the selection to that row alone, because a row is a button and activating it fires the click path
behaviours.dnd-start: Control+Shift+D picks up the selected rows, plus the focused one when it is not among them
behaviours.dnd-arrows-drive-the-drag: while a drag is up the arrows move the DROP TARGET and not the focus — the ordinary arrow hotkeys switch themselves off
behaviours.dnd-focus-stays: the browser's focus does not move during a drag, though the roving tab stop does
behaviours.dnd-drop-moves: Enter drops, and the rows move to the target
behaviours.dnd-drop-focus: after a drop, focus is on the first row that was carried
behaviours.dnd-escape-cancels: Escape ends the drag and moves nothing
behaviours.dnd-arrows-return-after-cancel: and the arrows work again afterwards, from where the drag left the tab stop rather than from where it began
behaviours.dnd-pointer-bands: where in a row's HEIGHT the cursor sits picks the target: the top band is above, the bottom band below, the middle drops INTO the row
behaviours.dnd-pointer-no-middle: a row nothing may be dropped into has no middle at all — the bands grow from 30% to 50% and meet
behaviours.dnd-pointer-open-folder-takes-children: an OPEN folder takes children from anywhere below its top band, including the bottom of the row where an ordinary row would reorder below
behaviours.dnd-pointer-reparent: far left on the LAST row of a group reparents — how far in the cursor is picks which ancestor's level the row lands at
behaviours.dnd-pointer-reparent-floor: and never further out than the row BELOW, so the level the cursor asks for is a floor and not an answer
behaviours.dnd-pointer-overwrites-selection: grabbing a row that is not selected REPLACES the selection with it, unlike the keyboard's start which adds to it

dnd-pointer-keeps-last-target.note: moving over a row nothing can be dropped on leaves the previous target standing rather than clearing it

dnd-pointer-drag-code.note: a move is ignored when its DRAG CODE has not changed — and the code is computed as if the row could take a child, so on a row that cannot, two heights either side of the middle are one code and the second move is swallowed

behaviours.dnd-pointer-drop-recomputes: the drop computes its own target from its own coordinates, so it can land where the line was not
behaviours.dnd-pointer-auto-open: holding a drag over a CLOSED folder opens it after 800ms, so a drop can reach somewhere that was not visible when the drag began
behaviours.dnd-pointer-auto-open-needs-the-whole-de: and it is the whole 800ms from the first arrival: a repeat of the same move does not restart it, and leaving the row makes it decline
behaviours.dnd-pointer-auto-open-needs-a-target: a folder with nowhere to drop does not open, even while the cursor points into it

table.$comment: Not Radix — Radix has no table. ReUI's, and every shadcn-family one, is TanStack Table underneath, so TanStack is the oracle. It is a NARROWER oracle than dnd-kit: TanStack is headless and contributes no roles, no aria-sort and no announcements at all, so only the state machine below is copied from it and the ARIA comes from the HTML table spec. Captured in oracle/table.json.

behaviours.table-roles: the grid reports as a table of rows, column headers and cells
behaviours.sort-three-states: a header cycles first direction, other direction, then unsorted — not a two-way toggle
behaviours.sort-numeric-descends-first: a numeric column's first click sorts DESCENDING, a text column's ascending
behaviours.aria-sort: the sorted header exposes aria-sort and the others do not
behaviours.sort-resets-page: re-ordering puts you back on the first page — page two of the old order is a window onto rows that moved
behaviours.select-row: a row can be selected and says so with aria-selected
behaviours.select-all-page: the header checkbox selects and clears THIS PAGE's rows, leaving others alone
behaviours.select-all-mixed: the header checkbox is mixed when some but not all of the page is selected
behaviours.page-next-prev: paging moves a window over the rows and reports how many pages there are
behaviours.page-edges: the paging controls are disabled at the ends rather than running past them

resizable.$comment: Not Radix — Radix has no resizable. ReUI's is react-resizable-panels, and its own prop names give it away: `orientation` and percentage STRINGS ("50%") are that library's API and nobody else's. The whole contract is DOM-observable — role, four ARIA attributes and a keyboard — so this is ordinary conformance with no bespoke capture, unlike the tree's drop targets or the table's state machine. The library gives the separator NO accessible name; the playground supplies one on both sides, because an unnamed focusable control is an omission rather than a contract — see `separator-unnamed`.

behaviours.separator-role: the draggable divider is a separator, and the panels and the group carry no role at all
behaviours.separator-orientation-inverts: a separator in a HORIZONTAL group says aria-orientation=vertical, because the attribute describes the separator LINE and not the axis it resizes
behaviours.separator-value-is-the-panel-before: aria-valuenow is the percentage size of the panel immediately BEFORE the separator, so moving one separator changes the next one's value too
behaviours.separator-tabstop: every separator is its own tab stop — there is no roving tab stop and no single entry point
behaviours.separator-unnamed: the LIBRARY names no separator, which leaves a focusable control announcing "50, separator" and nothing about what it splits. That is an omission and not a contract, so both sides here name it after the panel it resizes — the one place this component diverges from what the reference ships, and it diverges by adding rather than by changing
behaviours.separator-arrows: the arrows along the group's axis move the divider by five percent a press
behaviours.separator-arrows-wrong-axis: and the other pair does nothing at all — the key handler reads the GROUP's orientation, which is the opposite of the one the separator publishes
behaviours.separator-home-end: Home and End are deltas of a hundred rather than absolute ends, which only shows when constraints clamp them short

separator-constraints.note: aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax are what the LAYOUT allows for that panel, not what the panel asked for
separator-constraints.disputed: Only in a group of TWO. From three panels up the reference publishes an incoherent range on every separator but the first: measured at 20/30/50, the second separator says aria-valuemin=50, aria-valuenow=30, aria-valuemax=0 — min above now above max, and valuemin tracking the CUMULATIVE size up to that panel rather than any minimum. No assistive technology can use that, so this side publishes a coherent range and diverges on purpose; `resizable_f6` lists the two fields in its `ignore` and says why. The two-panel case, where the reference is right, is measured in full.

behaviours.separator-enter-collapses: Enter collapses the panel BEFORE the separator, and only when that panel is collapsible
behaviours.separator-enter-restores: and Enter again puts it back to the size it had, not to its minimum
behaviours.separator-f6-cycles: F6 walks to the next separator in the SAME group and wraps; Shift+F6 goes back. In a nested layout each group has one, so F6 lands where it started
